discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 0a13417b. Unix status commands now run in dedicated process groups that are killed on completion/cancellation. Windows commands start suspended, are assigned to a KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE job before their primary thread resumes, and therefore cannot spawn descendants outside the job. Added a reload-cancellation regression test that verifies a descendant cannot survive.

I’m keeping this best-effort on the existing bounded application-event channel. Blocking the PTY reader when the UI loop is under pressure can stall terminal output or deadlock against pane work; adding a reliable side-effect queue would be a broader transport-policy change than BEL forwarding.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed the double restore in b93ce6e. The panic hook and `TerminalGuard::drop` now share one `Arc<AtomicBool>`, claimed at the top of `restore_terminal_state`, so the first caller wins and the second returns early. I put the latch on the guard rather than in a process-wide static so a second client session in the same process still restores its own state. Added a test that two claims through the same latch only admit one.

On the partial-setup point: it is real, but it predates this branch and this patch does not widen it. `push_keyboard_enhancement_flags()?` is followed by the `modify_other_keys` write, `execute!(DisableLineWrap)`, and the Windows win32-input-mode block, so a failure in any of those returns `Err` before the guard exists and nothing pops — same on master. I have left it out to keep this PR to the detach bug. Happy to send a separate PR with a setup-scoped guard if you want it.

The startup query — the path that matters for the WSL bug — is fully protected. For resize re-queries, arming per query needs a main-loop-to-reader channel (the framer lives on the stdin thread), and whether the resize re-query stays at all is a design question the PR description explicitly leaves to the maintainers (attach-only vs. re-query on resize). Also worth noting the sibling thread on this review concluded the current behavior matches the host color query model, which likewise arms only from framer-observable events. If the maintainers want to keep the resize re-query, I'm happy to add a shared outstanding-replies counter so every query arms the hold.

Implemented in 741572b3. Every `CSI 16 t` emission now increments a shared pending-queries counter on the main loop (before the query reaches stdout), and the stdin reader drains that counter into the framer before framing each read and before the idle-flush decision, accumulating outstanding replies instead of resetting them. Tests cover two concurrent outstanding queries, re-arming after the first reply, and counter saturation.
Fixed in 4b06a614: the readiness handshake now uses a two-second `recv_timeout` and returns a timed-out error instead of blocking client notification handling indefinitely.

This preserves the existing headless backpressure policy rather than introducing a new loss path: before this refactor, committed text was converted to a semantic key and reached the same `try_send_bytes` call used by keys and paste. Retrying only `TextCommit` asynchronously would let later keys or releases overtake it. Correcting this requires one ordered headless input queue for text, keys, and paste, which is separate from this lifecycle refactor.
